```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)

source(here::here("R", "02b_extend_panel_2526.R"))

INK    <- "#1a1a2e"
PURPLE <- "#361a54"
BRIGHT <- "#993bff"
WARM   <- "#f56300"
GREY   <- "#666688"

theme_note <- function(base = 13) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base) +
    theme(
      plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", colour = PURPLE),
      plot.subtitle    = element_text(colour = GREY, size = rel(0.9)),
      axis.title       = element_text(colour = GREY, size = rel(0.9)),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
}

p5_path <- here::here("data", "panel_data_5yr.rds")
p5 <- if (file.exists(p5_path)) readRDS(p5_path) else extend_panel_2526()

# The EES institution-level file carries 2023/24 to 2025/26, so year-on-year
# comparisons are made inside it rather than against the panel, whose 2024/25
# came from the provisional performance tables.
e25 <- ees_ks4_year(202425L)
e26 <- ees_ks4_year(202526L)

yoy <- inner_join(
  e25 |> select(URN, SCHNAME, LANAME, a25 = ATT8SCR, d25 = ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A,
                n25 = ATT8SCR_NFSM6CLA1A),
  e26 |> select(URN, a26 = ATT8SCR, d26 = ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A,
                n26 = ATT8SCR_NFSM6CLA1A, f26 = PTFSM6CLA1A),
  by = "URN") |>
  mutate(chg = a26 - a25, chg_dis = d26 - d25, chg_ndis = n26 - n25)

fmt <- function(x, d = 2) sprintf(paste0("%+.", d, "f"), x)
```

::: callout-note
## Status

The 2025/26 Key Stage 4 figures used here are **provisional**, published by
the Department for Education on 15 October 2026. Revised figures follow in
February 2027. Nothing below should be treated as settled until they arrive.
:::

# What arrived, and why the pipeline had to change

The 2025/26 release brings a fifth year of Key Stage 4 results. It also
brings the end of the route this project used to get them.

> "Compare school and college performance (CSCP) will close soon. From autumn
> 2026, you will be able to use a new service. Data on CSCP will not be
> updated past the 2024/25 academic year."

`R/00_download_cscp.R` can therefore fetch 2021/22 to 2024/25 and nothing
after it. It is kept exactly as it is, because every published figure for
those four years reproduces from the files it fetched. From 2025/26 the data
comes instead from Explore Education Statistics, through
`R/00b_download_ees_api.R`, and is shaped into a panel year by
`R/01b_extract_ees_2526.R`.

Three things are genuinely absent from the new year, and all three are carried
as explicit gaps rather than quietly filled:

| Missing | Why | Consequence |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **Progress 8** | The 2025/26 cohort has no Key Stage 2 baseline — the 2019/20 and 2020/21 primary assessments were cancelled, and DfE confirmed no replacement measure | Already true of 2024/25; the reduced "core" specification was built for exactly this |
| **Prior attainment** | Same cause | `PTPRIORLO` / `PTPRIORHI` are `NA`, as in 2024/25 |
| **Full-year absence** | 2025/26 full-year absence publishes around March 2027 | Handled below — and it is the one that mattered |

# Is the new source the same as the old one?

The EES institution-level file covers 2023/24 to 2025/26, so it overlaps the
panel by two years. If the mapping from the EES long format onto the panel's
column names is right, the overlap should agree.

```{r validate}
#| tbl-cap: "EES institution-level data against the CSCP performance tables, on the years both cover"
panel4 <- readRDS(here::here("data", "panel_data.rds")) |>
  mutate(URN = as.character(URN))

cmp <- function(tp, ay) {
  e <- ees_ks4_year(tp) |>
    select(URN, e_att8 = ATT8SCR, e_dis = ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A,
           e_ndis = ATT8SCR_NFSM6CLA1A, e_fsm = PTFSM6CLA1A)
  p <- panel4 |> filter(academic_year == ay) |>
    select(URN, p_att8 = ATT8SCR, p_dis = ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A,
           p_ndis = ATT8SCR_NFSM6CLA1A, p_fsm = PTFSM6CLA1A)
  d <- inner_join(e, p, by = "URN")
  purrr::map_dfr(
    c(att8 = "Attainment 8", dis = "Disadvantaged",
      ndis = "Not disadvantaged", fsm = "Disadvantaged share"),
    function(lab) {
      v <- names(which(c(att8 = "Attainment 8", dis = "Disadvantaged",
                         ndis = "Not disadvantaged",
                         fsm = "Disadvantaged share") == lab))
      a <- d[[paste0("e_", v)]]; b <- d[[paste0("p_", v)]]
      ok <- !is.na(a) & !is.na(b)
      tibble(Year = ay, Measure = lab, Schools = sum(ok),
             r = round(cor(a[ok], b[ok]), 4),
             `Mean difference` = round(mean(a[ok] - b[ok]), 3),
             `Agree exactly` = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(abs(a[ok] - b[ok]) < 0.05)))
    })
}

bind_rows(cmp(202324L, "2023-2024"), cmp(202425L, "2024-2025"))
```

It does: correlations of 0.9998 to 1.0000 on every measure. The mapping is
sound.

The second row group is the more interesting one. For 2023/24 the two sources
agree exactly for about nine schools in ten; for 2024/25 only about three in
ten, with the EES figures running a shade higher. That is not an error — it is
the **provisional-to-revised revision**. The panel's 2024/25 came from
`england_ks4provisional.csv`; the EES file now carries the revised figures,
which include late results and the amendments schools requested. The same
thing will happen to the 2025/26 numbers in February 2027.

# The absence problem, and what to do about it

Absence is the strongest single predictor in the Lever model, and the centre
of its argument. Full-year absence for 2025/26 does not exist yet.

What does exist is a school-level file running **2016/17 to 2025/26** covering
the **autumn and spring terms** — every year of the panel, on one consistent
basis, reaching the new year. Summer term absence is excluded, so it is a
different quantity from `PERCTOT` and is carried as a separate variable,
`PERCTOT_2term`, never joined onto the old one.

```{r absence-compare}
#| fig-cap: "Full-year and autumn+spring absence, for the school-years where both are published"
both <- p5 |> filter(!is.na(PERCTOT), !is.na(PERCTOT_2term))
r_abs <- cor(both$PERCTOT, both$PERCTOT_2term)
d_abs <- mean(both$PERCTOT_2term - both$PERCTOT)

ggplot(both, aes(PERCTOT, PERCTOT_2term)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "grey60", linetype = "31") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.12, colour = PURPLE, size = 0.7) +
  labs(x = "Overall absence, full academic year (%)",
       y = "Overall absence, autumn + spring (%)",
       title = "The two absence bases measure nearly the same thing",
       subtitle = sprintf("%s school-years, r = %.3f, autumn+spring running %.2f points lower on average",
                          format(nrow(both), big.mark = ","), r_abs, d_abs)) +
  theme_note()
```

They are close: `r sprintf("r = %.3f", r_abs)` across
`r format(nrow(both), big.mark = ",")` school-years, with the two-term figure
`r sprintf("%.2f", abs(d_abs))` percentage points lower on average — summer
term absence is the higher part of the year, so dropping it pulls the number
down slightly and almost uniformly.

# Does the conclusion survive?

The question worth asking is not "can a fifth year be added" but "does adding
it change the answer". Three fits separate the two things that could move the
result — the change of absence basis, and the extra year.

```{r fits}
#| cache: true
fit_core <- function(d, absvar) {
  d <- d |>
    filter(!is.na(ATT8SCR), ATT8SCR > 0,
           !is.na(.data[[absvar]]), .data[[absvar]] > 0,
           !is.na(PTFSM6CLA1A), PTFSM6CLA1A > 0,
           !is.na(PNUMEAL), PNUMEAL > 0,
           !is.na(ADMPOL_PT), !is.na(gorard_segregation),
           !is.na(OFSTEDRATING_1), !is.na(gor_name), !is.na(LANAME))
  f <- as.formula(sprintf(paste(
    "log(ATT8SCR) ~ log(PTFSM6CLA1A) + log(%s) + log(PNUMEAL) +",
    "ADMPOL_PT + gorard_segregation +",
    "(1 | year_label) + (1 | OFSTEDRATING_1) + (1 | gor_name/LANAME)"), absvar))
  m <- lmer(f, data = d, REML = TRUE,
            control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa",
                                  optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)))
  list(m = m, n = nrow(d), co = summary(m)$coefficients)
}

four <- filter(p5, academic_year != "2025-2026")
A <- fit_core(four, "PERCTOT")
B <- fit_core(four, "PERCTOT_2term")
C <- fit_core(p5,   "PERCTOT_2term")

pull <- function(r, pat) {
  rn <- grep(pat, rownames(r$co), value = TRUE)[1]
  c(est = r$co[rn, "Estimate"], se = r$co[rn, "Std. Error"])
}
```

```{r fits-table}
#| tbl-cap: "The core specification, fitted three ways"
tibble(
  Fit = c("A. Published baseline", "B. Absence basis swapped", "C. Fifth year added"),
  Years = c("2021/22–2024/25", "2021/22–2024/25", "2021/22–2025/26"),
  Absence = c("Full year", "Autumn + spring", "Autumn + spring"),
  `School-years` = format(c(A$n, B$n, C$n), big.mark = ","),
  `Absence coefficient` = sprintf("%.4f", c(pull(A, "PERCTOT")["est"],
                                            pull(B, "PERCTOT")["est"],
                                            pull(C, "PERCTOT")["est"])),
  `Disadvantage coefficient` = sprintf("%.4f", c(pull(A, "PTFSM6CLA1A")["est"],
                                                 pull(B, "PTFSM6CLA1A")["est"],
                                                 pull(C, "PTFSM6CLA1A")["est"]))
)
```

```{r coef-plot}
#| fig-cap: "Absence and disadvantage coefficients across the three fits, with 95% intervals"
#| fig-height: 3.4
fits  <- list(`A. Published\nbaseline` = A,
              `B. Absence basis\nswapped` = B,
              `C. Fifth year\nadded` = C)
terms <- c(Absence = "PERCTOT", Disadvantage = "PTFSM6CLA1A")

cf <- purrr::map_dfr(names(terms), function(tm) {
  purrr::map_dfr(names(fits), function(fn) {
    v <- pull(fits[[fn]], terms[[tm]])
    tibble(fit = fn, term = tm, est = unname(v["est"]), se = unname(v["se"]))
  })
}) |>
  mutate(fit = factor(fit, levels = names(fits)))

ggplot(cf, aes(est, fit, colour = term)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey70", linetype = "31") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = est - 1.96 * se, xmax = est + 1.96 * se),
                 height = 0.16, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Absence = BRIGHT, Disadvantage = WARM),
                      guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~ term, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Coefficient on log(x) in log(Attainment 8)", y = NULL,
       title = "Neither change moves the result",
       subtitle = "Elasticities: a 10% rise in absence costs about 2.6% of Attainment 8") +
  theme_note(12)
```

The absence elasticity goes
**`r sprintf("%.4f", pull(A,"PERCTOT")["est"])` → `r sprintf("%.4f", pull(B,"PERCTOT")["est"])` → `r sprintf("%.4f", pull(C,"PERCTOT")["est"])`**.
The disadvantage elasticity goes
**`r sprintf("%.4f", pull(A,"PTFSM6CLA1A")["est"])` → `r sprintf("%.4f", pull(B,"PTFSM6CLA1A")["est"])` → `r sprintf("%.4f", pull(C,"PTFSM6CLA1A")["est"])`**.

Every one of those moves is far inside the standard errors. Swapping the
absence basis is close to free, and a fifth year of data leaves the central
finding exactly where it was: **absence carries roughly twice the weight of
disadvantage**, and it is the variable policy has most purchase on.

That is the most useful thing a new year of data can do. It was a chance for
the conclusion to fail, and it did not.

# What actually changed in 2025/26

```{r england}
# Paired means only: a school missing either year would otherwise shift the
# two averages by different amounts and invent a change that is not there.
nat_all <- yoy |> filter(!is.na(a25), !is.na(a26))
nat_dis <- yoy |> filter(!is.na(d25), !is.na(d26), !is.na(n25), !is.na(n26))
nat <- tibble(
  n   = nrow(nat_all),
  a25 = mean(nat_all$a25), a26 = mean(nat_all$a26),
  d25 = mean(nat_dis$d25), d26 = mean(nat_dis$d26),
  n25 = mean(nat_dis$n25), n26 = mean(nat_dis$n26))
gap25 <- nat$n25 - nat$d25; gap26 <- nat$n26 - nat$d26
```

Across `r format(nat$n, big.mark = ",")` matched state-funded mainstream
schools in England, headline Attainment 8 was **flat**: a change of
`r fmt(nat$a26 - nat$a25)` points. Underneath it, something more interesting:

- disadvantaged pupils **`r fmt(nat$d26 - nat$d25)`**, from `r sprintf("%.1f", nat$d25)` to `r sprintf("%.1f", nat$d26)`
- everyone else **`r fmt(nat$n26 - nat$n25)`**, from `r sprintf("%.1f", nat$n25)` to `r sprintf("%.1f", nat$n26)`
- the **disadvantage gap narrowed by `r sprintf("%.2f", gap25 - gap26)` points**, from `r sprintf("%.2f", gap25)` to `r sprintf("%.2f", gap26)`

A flat headline hiding a narrowing gap is precisely the pattern a measure
built on averages is bad at showing, and precisely the one that matters.

## Brighton and Hove

```{r brighton}
#| tbl-cap: "Brighton and Hove state-funded secondary schools, 2024/25 to 2025/26 (provisional)"
bh <- yoy |>
  filter(LANAME == "Brighton and Hove", !is.na(f26)) |>
  arrange(desc(chg)) |>
  transmute(School = SCHNAME,
            `A8 2024/25` = a25, `A8 2025/26` = a26, Change = chg,
            `Disadvantaged 2024/25` = d25, `Disadvantaged 2025/26` = d26,
            `Disadvantaged change` = chg_dis,
            `Disadvantaged %` = f26)
bh
```

The city moved **`r fmt(mean(bh$Change, na.rm = TRUE))` points** against a
national change of `r fmt(nat$a26 - nat$a25)`. Two movements stand out, and
they are in opposite directions.

```{r lh-baca}
#| fig-cap: "Longhill and Brighton Aldridge, against the national distribution of Attainment 8"
pctile <- function(v, x) 100 * mean(v <= x, na.rm = TRUE)
lh <- yoy |> filter(SCHNAME == "Longhill High School")
bc <- yoy |> filter(SCHNAME == "Brighton Aldridge Community Academy")

mk <- tibble(
  school = rep(c("Longhill", "Brighton Aldridge"), each = 2),
  year   = rep(c("2024/25", "2025/26"), 2),
  a8     = c(lh$a25, lh$a26, bc$a25, bc$a26))

ggplot(yoy |> select(a26) |> filter(!is.na(a26)), aes(a26)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "grey85") +
  geom_vline(data = mk, aes(xintercept = a8, colour = school,
                            linetype = year), linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Longhill = BRIGHT,
                                 `Brighton Aldridge` = WARM)) +
  labs(x = "Attainment 8, 2025/26", y = "Schools", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL,
       title = "Longhill up, Brighton Aldridge down — they have crossed",
       subtitle = sprintf(paste(
         "Longhill %.1f to %.1f, rising past %.0f%% to %.0f%% of schools in England;",
         "Brighton Aldridge %.1f to %.1f, falling from above %.0f%% to above %.0f%%"),
         lh$a25, lh$a26, pctile(yoy$a25, lh$a25), pctile(yoy$a26, lh$a26),
         bc$a25, bc$a26, pctile(yoy$a25, bc$a25), pctile(yoy$a26, bc$a26))) +
  theme_note()
```

**Longhill rose `r fmt(lh$chg, 1)` points** and its disadvantaged pupils rose
`r fmt(lh$chg_dis, 1)`. **Brighton Aldridge fell `r fmt(bc$chg, 1)`**, with its
disadvantaged pupils falling `r fmt(bc$chg_dis, 1)`. On the headline measure
the two schools have swapped places.

## Did Brighton Aldridge simply take a harder intake?

That is the first thing to rule out, and the answer is no — the composition
moved the other way.

```{r composition}
#| tbl-cap: "Cohort composition and scores, three years"
comp <- bind_rows(
  ees_ks4_year(202324L) |> mutate(Year = "2023/24"),
  e25 |> mutate(Year = "2024/25"),
  e26 |> mutate(Year = "2025/26")) |>
  filter(SCHNAME %in% c("Longhill High School",
                        "Brighton Aldridge Community Academy")) |>
  transmute(School = ifelse(grepl("Aldridge", SCHNAME),
                            "Brighton Aldridge", "Longhill"),
            Year, Cohort = TPUP,
            `Disadvantaged %` = PTFSM6CLA1A,
            `A8 all` = ATT8SCR,
            `A8 disadvantaged` = ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A,
            `A8 not disadvantaged` = ATT8SCR_NFSM6CLA1A) |>
  mutate(`Internal gap` = `A8 not disadvantaged` - `A8 disadvantaged`) |>
  arrange(School, Year)
comp
```

```{r baca-numbers}
b25 <- comp |> filter(School == "Brighton Aldridge", Year == "2024/25")
b26 <- comp |> filter(School == "Brighton Aldridge", Year == "2025/26")
l25 <- comp |> filter(School == "Longhill", Year == "2024/25")
l26 <- comp |> filter(School == "Longhill", Year == "2025/26")

# How far outside the normal range is a move of that size, for a
# disadvantaged cohort of that size?
nat_dis <- inner_join(
  e25 |> select(URN, SCHNAME, d25 = ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A),
  e26 |> select(URN, d26 = ATT8SCR_FSM6CLA1A, t26 = TFSM6CLA1A),
  by = "URN") |>
  filter(!is.na(d25), !is.na(d26)) |>
  mutate(chg = d26 - d25)
bc_chg <- nat_dis$chg[nat_dis$SCHNAME == "Brighton Aldridge Community Academy"]
peer <- nat_dis |> filter(!is.na(t26), t26 >= 60, t26 < 80)
```

Brighton Aldridge's cohort **grew**, from `r b25$Cohort` to `r b26$Cohort`,
and its disadvantaged share **fell**, from
`r sprintf("%.1f%%", b25[["Disadvantaged %"]])` to
`r sprintf("%.1f%%", b26[["Disadvantaged %"]])`. A smaller disadvantaged share
should push the headline score *up*. Its non-disadvantaged pupils also did
better, `r sprintf("%.1f to %.1f", b25[["A8 not disadvantaged"]], b26[["A8 not disadvantaged"]])`.

The headline fell anyway, because the disadvantaged half of the school fell
`r sprintf("%.1f", abs(bc_chg))` points. **The gap between the two groups
inside the school went from `r sprintf("%.1f", b25[["Internal gap"]])` points
to `r sprintf("%.1f", b26[["Internal gap"]])`** in a single year.

Longhill moved in the opposite direction on every line: disadvantaged share
down from `r sprintf("%.1f%%", l25[["Disadvantaged %"]])` to
`r sprintf("%.1f%%", l26[["Disadvantaged %"]])`, both groups up, and its
internal gap narrowing from `r sprintf("%.1f", l25[["Internal gap"]])` to
`r sprintf("%.1f", l26[["Internal gap"]])`.

```{r peer-check}
#| fig-cap: "Year-on-year change in disadvantaged Attainment 8, schools with 60-79 disadvantaged pupils"
#| fig-height: 3.2
ggplot(peer, aes(chg)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 45, fill = "grey85") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = bc_chg, colour = WARM, linewidth = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = bc_chg, y = Inf, label = "  Brighton Aldridge",
           colour = WARM, hjust = 0, vjust = 1.6, size = 3.6) +
  labs(x = "Change in disadvantaged Attainment 8, 2024/25 to 2025/26",
       y = "Schools",
       title = "Not the ordinary noise of a small cohort",
       subtitle = sprintf("%s schools with a disadvantaged cohort the same size as Brighton Aldridge's; SD %.1f points, %.0f%% move more than 10",
                          format(nrow(peer), big.mark = ","), sd(peer$chg),
                          100 * mean(abs(peer$chg) > 10))) +
  theme_note(12)
```

Small cohorts do swing. But for schools with a disadvantaged cohort the size
of Brighton Aldridge's, the standard deviation of year-on-year change is
`r sprintf("%.1f", sd(peer$chg))` points and only
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(abs(peer$chg) > 10))` move by more than ten.
Brighton Aldridge's `r sprintf("%.1f", bc_chg)` sits at the
`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * mean(nat_dis$chg <= bc_chg))`th percentile of all
`r format(nrow(nat_dis), big.mark = ",")` schools nationally. Whatever it is,
it is not the usual noise.

::: callout-warning
## Do not over-read this yet

Three reasons for caution, all of them real:

1. **These are provisional figures.** February's revisions will move them.
2. **One year.** The composition check above rules out the easy explanation,
   and the peer comparison rules out ordinary small-cohort noise — but a
   single cohort can still be unusual for reasons no published table shows.
   The thing to do is look again in February, and again in 2027.
3. **Attainment 8 is not value added.** The simulator's third policy lever —
   "what if Longhill added value like Brighton Aldridge" — rests on a
   four-year value-added measure, not on one year of headline scores. A
   single year's Attainment 8 cannot overturn it.

What this *does* justify is re-running the value-added measure with the new
year in it, and seeing whether the gap that lever depends on is still there.
:::

# The value-added measure, re-run

Attainment 8 describes an intake. The measure the Brighton work actually
leans on is **value added** — what a school adds once its intake is accounted
for, taken as the residual of the fitted model: observed Attainment 8 minus
what the model expects, averaged over the panel years.

The published version uses the *imputed full* specification, which needs
workforce variables that do not exist for 2025/26. So this refits the **core**
specification — the five predictors present in every year — and checks the two
agree before extending anything.

```{r va-fit}
#| cache: true
core_rhs <- paste("log(PTFSM6CLA1A) + log(%s) + log(PNUMEAL) +",
                  "ADMPOL_PT + gorard_segregation +",
                  "(1 | year_label) + (1 | OFSTEDRATING_1) + (1 | gor_name/LANAME)")

fit_resid <- function(d, absvar) {
  keep <- d |>
    filter(!is.na(ATT8SCR), ATT8SCR > 0, !is.na(.data[[absvar]]), .data[[absvar]] > 0,
           !is.na(PTFSM6CLA1A), PTFSM6CLA1A > 0, !is.na(PNUMEAL), PNUMEAL > 0,
           !is.na(ADMPOL_PT), !is.na(gorard_segregation),
           !is.na(OFSTEDRATING_1), !is.na(gor_name), !is.na(LANAME))
  m <- lmer(as.formula(sprintf(paste("log(ATT8SCR) ~", core_rhs), absvar)),
            data = keep, REML = TRUE,
            control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)))
  # On the Attainment 8 scale, so it is comparable with the published measure
  keep$pred_a8  <- exp(predict(m, keep, allow.new.levels = TRUE))
  keep$resid_a8 <- keep$ATT8SCR - keep$pred_a8
  keep
}

r4 <- fit_resid(filter(p5, academic_year != "2025-2026"), "PERCTOT")
r5 <- fit_resid(p5, "PERCTOT_2term")

va_of <- function(d) d |> group_by(URN) |>
  summarise(va = mean(resid_a8, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

BHS <- file.path(dirname(here::here()), "bh_school_system", "data")
pub <- readRDS(file.path(BHS, "open_scenarios.rds"))$choice |>
  select(urn, school, pan, att8_pub = att8, va_pub = va) |>
  mutate(URN = as.character(urn))

vacmp <- pub |>
  left_join(va_of(r4) |> rename(va4 = va), by = "URN") |>
  left_join(va_of(r5) |> rename(va5 = va), by = "URN")
r_pub4 <- cor(vacmp$va_pub, vacmp$va4, use = "complete.obs")
```

Across the ten city schools the refitted core measure and the published one
agree at **r = `r sprintf("%.2f", r_pub4)`** on the same four years. Good, but
not identical — the core specification drops the workforce terms, so its
residuals sit on a slightly different level. Everything below therefore
compares **core-on-four-years with core-on-five-years**, like with like.

```{r va-table}
#| tbl-cap: "Value added per school: published, refitted on four years, and extended to five"
vacmp |>
  transmute(School = sub(" School$| High School$| Community Academy$| and Sixth Form Centre$",
                         "", school),
            `Published (imputed, 4yr)` = round(va_pub, 2),
            `Core, 4 years` = round(va4, 2),
            `Core, 5 years` = round(va5, 2),
            Shift = round(va5 - va4, 2)) |>
  arrange(desc(`Core, 5 years`))
```

## What it does to the third policy lever

The simulator's third lever asks what happens if Longhill's value added
doubled, "to roughly where Brighton Aldridge already is with a comparably
disadvantaged intake". That framing depends on a gap between the two schools.

```{r lever3}
lh <- vacmp |> filter(grepl("Longhill", school))
bc <- vacmp |> filter(grepl("Aldridge", school), !grepl("Portslade", school))
gap4 <- bc$va4 - lh$va4; gap5 <- bc$va5 - lh$va5
```

| | Longhill | Brighton Aldridge | Gap |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| Published (imputed, 4 years) | `r fmt(lh$va_pub)` | `r fmt(bc$va_pub)` | `r fmt(bc$va_pub - lh$va_pub)` |
| Core, 4 years | `r fmt(lh$va4)` | `r fmt(bc$va4)` | `r fmt(gap4)` |
| **Core, 5 years** | **`r fmt(lh$va5)`** | **`r fmt(bc$va5)`** | **`r fmt(gap5)`** |

The gap **`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * (1 - gap5 / gap4))` smaller** with the
new year in, and Brighton Aldridge's own value added has gone **negative**.
It is no longer a school beating what its intake predicts.

```{r va-years}
#| tbl-cap: "Year by year: what each school scored, what the model expected from its intake, and the difference"
r5 |>
  filter(URN %in% c(lh$URN, bc$URN)) |>
  transmute(School = ifelse(URN == lh$URN, "Longhill", "Brighton Aldridge"),
            Year = academic_year,
            `Attainment 8` = ATT8SCR,
            `Expected from intake` = round(pred_a8, 1),
            `Value added` = round(resid_a8, 2)) |>
  arrange(School, Year)
```

This table is the important one, and it says two things that the headline
scores do not.

**Brighton Aldridge's fall is entirely 2025/26.** For four years its value
added sat within half a point of zero — the school performing almost exactly
as its intake predicted. Then one year at
`r sprintf("%.2f", r5$resid_a8[r5$URN == bc$URN & r5$academic_year == "2025-2026"])`.

```{r lh-detail}
lhy <- r5 |> filter(URN == lh$URN) |>
  select(academic_year, ATT8SCR, pred_a8, resid_a8)
g <- function(y, v) lhy[[v]][lhy$academic_year == y]
```

**Longhill's rise is mostly its intake, not its teaching.** Its Attainment 8
went from `r sprintf("%.1f", g("2024-2025", "ATT8SCR"))` to
`r sprintf("%.1f", g("2025-2026", "ATT8SCR"))`. But the model *expected* it to
go from `r sprintf("%.1f", g("2024-2025", "pred_a8"))` to
`r sprintf("%.1f", g("2025-2026", "pred_a8"))`, because its disadvantaged
share fell from 40.1% to 33.5%. Measured against that, Longhill's value added
barely moved: `r sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", g("2024-2025", "resid_a8"), g("2025-2026", "resid_a8"))`.

So the two schools did not really move in opposite directions. **Longhill
stood still and got an easier intake; Brighton Aldridge fell.**

## And to the simulator's attractiveness term

```{r mult}
#| tbl-cap: "Attractiveness multipliers under the 'families read value added' scenario"
acc  <- readRDS(file.path(BHS, "accessibility.rds"))
fpan <- readRDS(file.path(BHS, "factsheet_panel.rds"))
oi   <- readRDS(file.path(BHS, "open_inputs.rds"))

w_cd <- fpan$factsheets |>
  filter(name != "Total", year >= max(year) - 4) |>
  group_by(name) |>
  summarise(p1 = mean(pref1), p2 = mean(pref2), p3 = mean(pref3), .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(oi$attract |> select(urn, name), by = "name") |>
  inner_join(pub |> select(urn, pan, att8_pub, va_pub), by = "urn") |>
  left_join(vacmp |> select(urn, va5), by = "urn") |>
  mutate(wpp = (p1 + acc$pref$decay * p2 + acc$pref$decay^2 * p3) / pan)

W_SLOPE <- coef(lm(log(wpp) ~ att8_pub, data = w_cd))[["att8_pub"]]
mult_from <- function(d, v) {
  eq  <- mean(d$att8_pub) + sd(d$att8_pub) * (d[[v]] - mean(d[[v]])) / sd(d[[v]])
  raw <- exp(W_SLOPE * (eq - d$att8_pub))
  raw / exp(mean(log(raw)))
}
w_cd$mult_pub <- mult_from(w_cd, "va_pub")
w_cd$mult_5yr <- mult_from(w_cd, "va5")

w_cd |>
  transmute(School = name,
            `As published` = round(mult_pub, 3),
            `With 2025/26` = round(mult_5yr, 3),
            Change = round(mult_5yr - mult_pub, 3)) |>
  arrange(desc(`As published`))
```

Reproducing the published arithmetic exactly (the `As published` column
matches the shipped multipliers to four decimal places), Brighton Aldridge's
multiplier falls from
**`r sprintf("%.2f", w_cd$mult_pub[grepl("Brighton Aldridge", w_cd$name)])`×
to `r sprintf("%.2f", w_cd$mult_5yr[grepl("Brighton Aldridge", w_cd$name)])`×**.
It was by a distance the biggest beneficiary of a switch to value added; it is
now one of several. Varndean, Dorothy Stringer and Blatchington Mill all gain.

::: callout-important
## What this means for the simulator, and what it does not

**The scenario still works.** "What if families read value added" remains a
real lever, and it still redistributes demand. But the *shape* of that
redistribution has changed, and the simulator's shipped multipliers are now
one year out of date.

**The third lever needs rewording, not retiring.** "Double Longhill's value
added" is still a coherent thing to model. "To roughly where Brighton
Aldridge already is" is no longer true on five years of data.

**One provisional year is doing all the work.** Brighton Aldridge sat within
half a point of zero for four years. Before rebuilding the simulator's
attractiveness on this, wait for February's revisions — a single year this
far out of line is exactly the case where a revision matters most.
:::

# Five years of Brighton and Hove, against England

Everything above is about one year. This is the series the new year joins:
the city's ten state-funded secondary schools from 2021/22 to 2025/26, on
both measures, with England drawn behind them.

```{r bh-series}
#| fig-cap: "Attainment 8, Brighton and Hove schools against the national distribution"
#| fig-height: 6.2
bh_urns <- pub$URN

eng_band <- r5 |>
  group_by(academic_year) |>
  summarise(med = median(ATT8SCR, na.rm = TRUE),
            lo  = quantile(ATT8SCR, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
            hi  = quantile(ATT8SCR, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

bh_series <- r5 |>
  filter(URN %in% bh_urns) |>
  left_join(pub |> select(URN, school), by = "URN") |>
  mutate(short = sub(" School$| High School$| Community Academy$| and Sixth Form Centre$",
                     "", school),
         yr = as.integer(substr(academic_year, 1, 4)) + 1L)

eng_band <- eng_band |> mutate(yr = as.integer(substr(academic_year, 1, 4)) + 1L)

ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = eng_band, aes(yr, ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
              fill = "grey88") +
  geom_line(data = eng_band, aes(yr, med), colour = "grey45",
            linetype = "31", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_line(data = bh_series, aes(yr, ATT8SCR), colour = PURPLE, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = bh_series, aes(yr, ATT8SCR), colour = PURPLE, size = 1.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ short, ncol = 5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2022:2026, labels = function(x) substr(x, 3, 4)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Attainment 8",
       title = "Attainment 8, 2021/22 to 2025/26",
       subtitle = "Grey band: the middle half of schools in England. Dashed line: the national median.") +
  theme_note(11)
```

```{r bh-va-series}
#| fig-cap: "Value added, Brighton and Hove schools. Zero is performing exactly as the intake predicts."
#| fig-height: 6.2
eng_va <- r5 |>
  group_by(academic_year) |>
  summarise(lo = quantile(resid_a8, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
            hi = quantile(resid_a8, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(yr = as.integer(substr(academic_year, 1, 4)) + 1L)

ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = eng_va, aes(yr, ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "grey88") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey45", linetype = "31", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_line(data = bh_series, aes(yr, resid_a8), colour = BRIGHT, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = bh_series, aes(yr, resid_a8), colour = BRIGHT, size = 1.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ short, ncol = 5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2022:2026, labels = function(x) substr(x, 3, 4)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Attainment 8 points above or below expectation",
       title = "Value added, 2021/22 to 2025/26",
       subtitle = "Grey band: the middle half of schools in England. Above zero is beating what the intake predicts.") +
  theme_note(11)
```

Read side by side, the two charts say different things about the same city.

On **Attainment 8** the schools are spread across the national distribution,
and the ordering barely changes from year to year — which is the point *How
to Pull the Right Lever* makes about the headline measure: it mostly restates
who walks through the door.

On **value added** the city is tighter and the movement is larger. A school
can sit in the bottom quarter of England on Attainment 8 and still be adding
what its intake predicts.

```{r bh-vs-eng}
#| fig-cap: "The city against England, both measures, pupil-weighted"
#| fig-height: 3.6
wmean <- function(x, w) sum(x * w, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(w[!is.na(x)], na.rm = TRUE)

agg <- bind_rows(
  r5 |> mutate(grp = ifelse(URN %in% bh_urns, "Brighton and Hove", "Rest of England")),
) |>
  group_by(grp, academic_year) |>
  summarise(att8 = wmean(ATT8SCR, TPUP), va = wmean(resid_a8, TPUP),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(yr = as.integer(substr(academic_year, 1, 4)) + 1L) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(att8, va), names_to = "measure", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(measure = factor(measure, c("att8", "va"),
                          c("Attainment 8", "Value added")))

ggplot(agg, aes(yr, value, colour = grp)) +
  geom_hline(data = tibble(measure = factor("Value added",
                                            levels = levels(agg$measure))),
             aes(yintercept = 0), colour = "grey70", linetype = "31") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) + geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ measure, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`Brighton and Hove` = BRIGHT,
                                 `Rest of England` = "grey55")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2022:2026, labels = function(x) substr(x, 3, 4)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL,
       title = "Brighton and Hove against the rest of England",
       subtitle = "Pupil-weighted means across state-funded mainstream schools") +
  theme_note(12) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r bh-agg-numbers}
a <- agg |> filter(grp == "Brighton and Hove")
e <- agg |> filter(grp == "Rest of England")
gv <- function(d, m, y) d$value[d$measure == m & d$yr == y]
```

Pupil-weighted, the city's Attainment 8 ran
`r sprintf("%.1f", gv(a, "Attainment 8", 2022))` in 2021/22 and
`r sprintf("%.1f", gv(a, "Attainment 8", 2026))` in 2025/26, against
`r sprintf("%.1f", gv(e, "Attainment 8", 2022))` and
`r sprintf("%.1f", gv(e, "Attainment 8", 2026))` for the rest of England. On
value added the city sat at
`r sprintf("%+.2f", gv(a, "Value added", 2022))` and
`r sprintf("%+.2f", gv(a, "Value added", 2026))`.

```{r bh-table}
#| tbl-cap: "Brighton and Hove schools, five years, both measures"
bh_series |>
  select(short, academic_year, ATT8SCR, resid_a8) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(ATT8SCR, resid_a8)) |>
  mutate(name = ifelse(name == "ATT8SCR", "A8", "VA"),
         col = paste0(substr(academic_year, 3, 4), "/",
                      substr(academic_year, 8, 9), " ", name)) |>
  select(School = short, col, value) |>
  mutate(value = round(value, 1)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = col, values_from = value) |>
  arrange(School)
```

# Where this leaves things

**Settled.** The new year can be added, the new source agrees with the old
one, and the central Lever finding is unchanged by both the extra year and
the change of absence basis.

**Open, and worth doing next:**

- Re-run the four-year value-added measure with 2025/26 in it. The Brighton
  simulator's attractiveness term $W_j$ and the third policy lever both
  depend on it, and Longhill and Brighton Aldridge have just moved in
  opposite directions.
- Decide whether to adopt the **revised** 2024/25 figures now available from
  EES in place of the provisional ones the published analysis used. The mean
  difference is about 0.12 Attainment 8 points.
- Revisit in February 2027, when 2025/26 is revised and the full-year absence
  series catches up.

**Reproducibility.** `data/panel_data.rds` is untouched: the published
four-year analysis still reproduces from exactly the files it was built on.
The five-year panel is written separately to `data/panel_data_5yr.rds` and
nothing adopts it until that is a deliberate decision.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
